### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | Use PCPartPicker.com to check compatibility and price. | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area | 1. Anti‑static wrist strap
2. Phillips screwdriver (size #2)
3. Small flathead screwdriver or pry tool
4. Cable ties or Velcro straps | | 3 | **Choose Components** | CPU, GPU, motherboard, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling | Stick to a single brand for the motherboard and CPU socket. | | 4 | **Open the Case** | Remove side panels | Unscrew the screws on the back of the case, slide panels off. | | 5 | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Provides power to all components | 1. Align the PSU fan with the case vent.
2. Secure with screws.
3. Route cables to the back. | | 6 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all components | 1. Install standoffs in the case to match the motherboard holes.
2. Align the I/O shield with the rear panel.
3. Screw the board in place. | | 7 | **Install the CPU** | Processor powers the system | 1. Lift the CPU socket lever.
2. Align the corner marker on the CPU with the socket.
3. Place gently, lower lever. | | 8 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating | 1. If cooler has pre‑applied paste, skip step 9.
2. Spread a pea‑size amount of paste on the CPU.
3. Attach cooler, tighten screws in a cross pattern. | | 9 | **Install RAM** | Memory for running programs | 1. Open the RAM slots by pushing the clips outward.
2. Align the notch on the stick with the slot key.
3. Push firmly until clips click. | |10 | **Install Storage (SSD/HDD)** | Drives for OS & data | 1. Mount SSD in 2.5” bay or M.2 slot.
2. Secure with screws or latch. | |11 | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Handles rendering for games & video | 1. Remove the appropriate PCIe slot cover on the case.
2. Insert GPU into the top PCIe x16 slot.
3. Secure with screws. | |12 | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components | 1. 24‑pin ATX to motherboard.
2. 8‑pin EPS to CPU.
3. 6/8‑pin PCIe to GPU.
4. SATA power to SSD/HDD. | |13 | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer | 1. SATA data cable to SSD/HDD.
2. M.2 connector if using NVMe. | |14 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow & aesthetics | 1. Route cables behind the motherboard tray.
2. Use ties or Velcro straps. | |15 | **Double‑Check Connections** | Prevent shorts & failures | Verify all screws, cables, and components are seated. | |16 | **Close the Case** | Protect components | Slide panels back, screw them in. | |17 | **First Boot & BIOS Setup** | Verify hardware & set boot order | 1. Connect monitor, keyboard, mouse.
2. Power on, enter BIOS (usually DEL or F2).
3. Check CPU, RAM, storage detection. | |18 | **Install Operating System** | Get your PC running | 1. Create a bootable USB with Windows 10/11 or Linux.
2. Boot from USB, follow installation wizard. | |19 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware works optimally | 1. Install motherboard chipset drivers.
2. Install GPU drivers from NVIDIA/AMD.
3. Run Windows Update. | |20 | **Test & Benchmark** | Confirm stability | 1. Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark).
2. Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor). | --- #### Quick Checklist - **Static Safety**: Wear wrist strap or touch metal part of case before handling components. - **Component Compatibility**: Verify CPU socket, motherboard chipset, RAM type, and PSU wattage. - **Cable Length**: Choose a PSU with enough cable length for your case layout. - **Cooling**: Consider additional case fans if you plan overclocking or have a high‑end GPU. - **Warranty**: Keep receipts and warranty cards; many components have 3‑year warranties. #### Common Pitfalls | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **CPU not seated** | Re‑align and re‑insert. | | **GPU not recognized** | Ensure 6/8‑pin power is connected; check BIOS for PCIe slot. | | **No POST** | Check power supply connections, remove all peripherals, test with minimal components. | | **Overheating** | Add case fans, improve cable routing, reapply thermal paste. | #### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community support. Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks: "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No function call needed.
